# CSV ANAXIMANDER — TECHNICAL OPERATIONAL SUMMARY

**TERRAN SURVEY INSTITUTE · CARTOGRAPHIC SURVEY DIVISION**
**Registry: ISC–CS–07 · Classification: RESTRICTED**

---

*Compiled by: Dr. Yara Solen, Senior Systems Engineer — Voss Fabrication Group*
*Revision 4.2 · Survey Division Archive, New Carthage Station · 15 Marthon 2851*

---

## 1. VESSEL OVERVIEW

The *Cartographic Survey Vessel Anaximander* (official designation ISC–CS–07) is a mid-weight, long-endurance survey corvette commissioned by the Terran Survey Institute in 2843. She is one of three vessels of the **Anaximander-class**, purpose-built for deep-field astronomical cartography and anomaly investigation beyond the Kepler Gap.


| Field                | Value                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Registry             | ISC–CS–07                                       |
| Class                | Anaximander (Survey Corvette)                   |
| Keel laid            | 14 Verath 2841                                  |
| Commissioned         | 03 Ostun 2843                                   |
| Shipyard             | Voss Fabrication Group, Io Station, Jovian Belt |
| Gross displacement   | 41,200 metric tonnes (dry)                      |
| Overall length       | 312 m                                           |
| Beam (max)           | 68 m                                            |
| Draft (max)          | 52 m                                            |
| Design endurance     | 36 months unresupplied                          |
| Crew (standard)      | 74 officers and crew                            |
| Scientific personnel | up to 22                                        |


*Disposition as of Revision 4.2: Active service. Currently assigned to Survey Region Tau-7 under mission TSI-SRT7-009.*

## 2. HULL CONFIGURATION

The Anaximander-class hull follows the split-ring truss design pioneered by Voss Group's earlier *Meridian*-class freighters, adapted for the stress profiles of repeated Alcubierre transitions. The primary hull is divided into five pressure rings (Α–Ε) separated by unpressurised strut frameworks to limit cascade decompression risk.

The forward sensor array (Ring Α) is rated for continuous operation within 0.4 AU of Class-G stars and certified to 0.15 AU at reduced duty cycles. The aft engineering section (Ring Ε) contains all primary drive components and is accessible only through hardsuit corridors during drive operation.

**Hull material:** T-9 Graphene-Tungsten laminate, 14 cm primary shell
**Radiation shielding:** Active magnetic field (Voss MagShield IV) + passive boron-carbide inner skin
**Thermal rejection:** 6 × Cascading Radiator Arrays, each 44 m span

## 3. PROPULSION SYSTEMS

### 3.1 Sublight Drive

Two **Meridian-Nyx Mk.III** ion-plasma drives provide sublight thrust rated at 2.4 MN each. Nominal acceleration at standard loadout: 0.18 g sustained. Emergency maximum: 0.31 g (limited to 40-minute bursts by thermal constraint).

Reaction mass: deuterium slush — primary tanks 8,400 m³, auxiliary tanks 1,100 m³.
Estimated ΔV reserve at departure (standard mission profile): 38.4 km/s.

### 3.2 Alcubierre-Novikov Warp Drive

The AN Drive fitted to ISC–CS–07 is a **Vorontsov-Langley AN-17C** — the fourth-generation variant, incorporating the corrected metric stability matrices first published by Dr. Feyre Andas of the Kepler Institute in 2838. Earlier AN-17 variants were responsible for the *Meridian Station Incident* of 2836; the 17C line has since logged over 2,400 combined warp-hours without a metric collapse event.


| Parameter                       | Value                             |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Warp factor range               | 0.5 – 9.2 (Kepler scale)          |
| Nominal transit warp            | 7.4                               |
| Maximum rated warp              | 8.8 (&lt; 72 hr continuous)       |
| Field coil material             | Exotic-state ferrite, ESF-4 grade |
| Field coil replacement interval | every 6,200 warp-hours            |
| Min. safe engagement distance   | 2.2 × 10⁶ km from stellar bodies  |
| Power draw at nominal warp      | 98 GW (primary fusion plant)      |


> **Note (Y.S.):** The AN drive on this hull has been modified — see §6.3. The Vorontsov-Langley stock configuration assumes a maximum exotic matter reservoir of 14 kg-equiv. Our refit expanded this to 22 kg-equiv, extending maximum warp endurance by approximately 31%. TSI Engineering Review Board approved this modification under waiver TSI-ERB-2849-0041. I remain mildly concerned about harmonic stress accumulation in Ring Ε strut C-7 during sustained factor-8+ transits. Monitoring recommended.

### 3.3 Attitude Control

28 × attitude control thrusters (hydrazine-derivative, 12 kN each) arranged in clusters at Rings Α, Γ, and Ε. Standard fit for class.

## 4. POWER SYSTEMS


| System            | Type                                        | Output                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Primary plant     | Inertial confinement fusion — Paladin Mk.II | 110 GW                       |
| Secondary plant   | Magnetohydrodynamic — Solis Compact MHD     | 14 GW                        |
| Emergency reserve | Graphene supercapacitor array               | 72 hr (minimal life support) |
| Fuel              | D-T pellet — 420-day supply at nominal      | —                            |


The primary Paladin Mk.II fusion plant was retrofitted in 2848 (Ring Ε, bay 3). The original Halcyon Series-7 plant logged a plasma containment anomaly during mission TSI-SRT4-003 traced to micro-fractures in the first-wall lining. The Paladin Mk.II has performed without incident since installation.

## 5. SURVEY AND SCIENTIFIC SYSTEMS

### 5.1 Primary Sensor Array (Ring Α)

- **ARTEMIS-9 Long-Range Interferometric Array** — 84 m baseline, operational 0.1 nm to 3 cm wavelength
- **Tidal Gradient Mapper TGM-22** — gravitational gradient detection to 10⁻¹⁸ m/s² sensitivity; capable of resolving concealed mass concentrations at distances up to 4 AU
- **Deep Neutrino Spectrometer DNS-5** — distinguishes artificial neutrino emission profiles from stellar background; useful for locating dormant installations or exotic energy sources
- **Subspace Resonance Detector SRD-III** — detects metric distortions consistent with prior or active AN-drive activity within approximately 0.8 light-years

### 5.2 Autonomous Survey Probes

The *Anaximander* carries **12 × Alcyone Mk.IV** autonomous survey drones. Each is capable of independent operation for up to 90 days at ranges up to 0.4 AU. Each carries a miniaturised ARTEMIS-9 array.

Drone bay: Ring Γ (ventral). Recovery success rate across all missions to date: **94.4%**. Two drones were lost during TSI-SRT6-011 (see §7).

### 5.3 Scientific Laboratory Modules

Four interchangeable modules occupy Ring Γ (dorsal):


| Bay  | Current Module                              | Notes                                       |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Γ-L1 | Materials Analysis &amp; Sample Containment | Upgraded to BSL-3 equivalence, 2849         |
| Γ-L2 | Xenolinguistics &amp; Signal Processing     | Standard fit                                |
| Γ-L3 | Computational Physics — Warp Metrics        | Expanded processor cluster, non-standard    |
| Γ-L4 | **RESERVED — Anomaly Research**             | Contents classified under TSI Directive 7-Θ |


> **Note (Y.S.):** I have not been granted access to Γ-L4 since 2850. I am told this is routine for Directive 7-Θ rated work. I note it here for completeness. Any future engineering review of Ring Γ should be coordinated directly with Survey Division.

## 6. NOTABLE MODIFICATIONS AND NON-STANDARD COMPONENTS

### 6.1 Extended Endurance Tankage

Auxiliary deuterium tanks enlarged by 22% during the 2848 refit. Range at standard warp extended from approximately 1,100 light-years to approximately 1,340 light-years unresupplied.

### 6.2 Structural Reinforcement, Ring Β

Following micro-fracture detection during the 2847 pre-launch inspection, Ring Β received an additional T-9 laminate layer on the forward face and internal brace insertion at frames 14, 18, and 22. Mass penalty: +180 metric tonnes. Performance within normal operational parameters is unaffected.

### 6.3 AN Drive Exotic Matter Reservoir Expansion

*(See §3.2 above.)* Approved under waiver TSI-ERB-2849-0041. Reservoir expanded from 14 kg-equiv to 22 kg-equiv ESF-4 grade exotic matter.

**Caution:** do not engage warp above factor 8.4 for durations exceeding 18 hours without a full field coil inspection interval.

### 6.4 Quantum Entanglement Relay

A **Voss QER-2C** second-generation quantum entanglement relay was installed in 2850, replacing the standard laser-burst array as primary deep-field communications. Effective communications range: unlimited (entanglement-keyed). Latency: &lt; 0.8 ms one-way. Currently paired with New Carthage Station and Kepler Gate Relay 7.

## 8. ENGINEER'S OBSERVATIONS

*The following notes are the personal observations of Dr. Yara Solen, Senior Systems Engineer, and do not constitute official TSI documentation.*

The *Anaximander* is a capable vessel and I have worked with worse. The Paladin Mk.II fusion plant is, in my opinion, the single most reliable component aboard — I trust it more than the AN drive, more than the life support, and frankly more than some of the crew. The structural patch at Ring Β has held without measurable creep for four years; I no longer worry about it.

What I do think about, more than I used to, is Ring Ε strut C-7. Fourteen months into TSI-SRT6-011 I recorded a 0.003% harmonic deviation during a factor-8.2 transit. It fell within tolerance. I noted it, filed the report, received a form acknowledgment. On the next three transits it did not recur. But I wrote it here anyway, because instruments that deviate once tend to have reasons.

The signal logged during TSI-SRT5-018 was at 1420 MHz — the hydrogen line. Structured. Twelve repetitions of what the xenolinguistics team described as a "geometric primer sequence." We spent six weeks trying to locate the source. We never did. I was not present when the Directive 7-Θ order arrived during TSI-SRT6-011, but I was told the two occurrences are unrelated.

I have been told many things.
